text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 15

The panel's composition alone is weak evidence. Laboratory medicine and biomedical science are heavily female fields, so an all-women panel can easily arise by chance from whoever holds senior posts. Leading with it would make you look aggrieved rather than credible, and it's the easiest part of your case to dismiss.

What's actually worth pursuing: the unanswered request for written reasons. That's a concrete procedural failure. Send a polite follow-up, cite any applicable policy or statutory deadline, and copy HR.

Also consider that the panel may genuinely have weighted management credentials and leadership over research depth — common for department-head roles. If the reasons, once given, don't match the advertised criteria, that's your real argument.
